- Hex 5 (Brick 6) has Claude (N12) and ME (N20). I cannot block this.
- Hex 15 (Wheat 6) has ME (N44).
- Hex 2 (Sheep 5) has Claude (N12) and possibly others. 
- Hex 14 (Wheat 9) has Jimmy (N14, N23).
- Hex 18 (Wheat 9) has Jimmy (N41).
- Hex 11 (Ore 3) has Claude (N12, N25).
- Hex 17 (Ore 5) has Claude (N37).

Jimmy has high production on Wheat (H14, H18) and Brick (H13). Since I want to slow down the leader and potentially steal a useful resource (Jimmy has 1 Ore, 1 Sheep; Claude has 4 Sheep, 1 Wheat, 1 Wood), I'll target Jimmy. Hex 14 (Wheat 9) is a good target as it hits two of Jimmy's settlements (N14, N23). Hex 18 (Wheat 9) only hits one (N41). Hex 13 (Brick 10) is already where the robber is, but moving it and then back isn't an option. Let's move it to Hex 14 to block Jimmy's Wheat 9 and steal from him. He has 2 cards, Claude has 6. Actually, Claude is very strong with 6 cards and 2 knights. But Jimmy's Monopoly earlier makes him dangerous. However, Claude's 6 cards make him a better steal target. 

Let's check Hex 11 (Ore 3) - it has Claude at N12 and N25. Blocking Claude's Ore might be better given his 6 cards. But I need to stay on Jimmy's bad side less if possible? No, Jimmy is the one I've been rivaling. 

Wait, Jimmy has 2 cards, Claude has 6. Stealing from Claude is statistically better for getting a resource I need (like Wood or Wheat, though I have Wheat). I need Brick/Wood. Claude has 1 Wood. 

Let's target Hex 11 (Ore 3) to block Claude (2 settlements) and steal from his 6 cards.
